newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin fires tax head, railways minister.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin fires tax head, railways minister.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin dismissed the head of the tax service on Monday and replaced the railways minister and a deputy foreign minister, the Kremlin press service said.

The sackings were the latest steps in a far-reaching government reshuffle initiated by Yeltsin in February in a bid to give a new push to market reforms and policy which drifted while he suffered heart problems last year.
Vitaly Artyukhov, head of the Russian State Tax Service, resigned last week, saying his position had become unclear following a series of sweeping changes to the Russian government's economic team.
Many officials have blamed government budget woes and other problems on inefficient tax collection, which is more than 40 percent behind schedule this year.

Yeltsin did not name a replacement in his decree dismissing Artyuhkov, which, like those dealing with the other personnel changes, mentioned only that the officials were being dismissed "in connection with their transfer to other jobs."
Nikolai Aksenenko was appointed Railways Minister, replacing Anatoly Zaitsev, who had previously run the state rail system.
In a separate decree, Ivan Sergeyev, previously an administrator overseeing services to foreign diplomats in Russia, was named deputy foreign minister replacing Ivan Kuznetsov.

Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov has survived the reshuffle and even won praise from Yeltsin on Monday, but long-term presidential foreign policy aide Dmitry Rurikov was swept away in the wave of personnel changes.
